paper.title: Automated Rewards via LLM-Generated Progress Functions
paper.source_version: arXiv v2, submitted 2024-10-25, latest and active of two public revisions verified 2026-08-30; reviewed PDF SHA-256 15d2442bd8cdc9f382453f7c326435b4d64dca3554537995e456352f070d381e and source-tar SHA-256 8d076dd7ca114f8806c94c1a5584a8fb54894c9b7983df5a29fb632a97234fdf. Official anonymous LLMCount artifacts pinned by Drive file ID and exact bytes: BiDex 1J6ppChCMknLlJv_pv0uNi8f3sTL1owlW, 196809369 bytes, SHA-256 a024e43df908e521822d47354cd55be0dfebf1e1e66cea1b7b2162bfd660be6c; NovelD 1USyY4nHNTqXmS6Qj1fCHF7ggKmlW1KtA, 6573377 bytes, SHA-256 5bdc80e57e3c3ce2ab17baaf160d3bbe5b86dfe9a41a1c21337689a07f82e90f; Instructions 1b-_HBbrrX82sZmKpx2VPoo8cMpkvpUQ_2VbJt3RSvfY, exported-text SHA-256 452ed06d54ca9c5080cdea4aeb5394615567e4a20f658d4094156c8c69223f75. The Drive artifacts have no release tag or verified public commit.

decision_relevance.why_admitted: ProgressCounts is direct evidence for constructing an executable task reward from an LLM-generated low-dimensional progress projection plus count-based exploration. Its public implementation shows that the admitted reward artifact must include discretization, initialized extrema, global count state, update order, sparse-success semantics, live-batch normalization, and clipping; otherwise a nominally fixed trainer silently changes the reward mechanism.
not_evidence_for: reference-motion selection, ordering, transitions, blending, composition, or certification
a reference-conditioned actor or critic with an immutable playback clock
progress features serving as policy-conditioning observations
matched total outer-loop training compute in the TwoCatchUnderarm stretch result
an independent holdout evaluator for selecting among generated progress functions
safe execution of arbitrary LLM-generated Python with unrestricted simulator-self access
real-robot transfer, physical observation sufficiency, contact safety, naturalness, perturbation recovery, or calibrated confidence
a stateless reward function that can be swapped into any frozen trainer
a complete versioned public reproduction of the GPT progress-generation stage and all reported tables

mechanisms.name: LLM progress-function generator
mechanisms.description: Given a short task description, simulator state-feature description, and a small benchmark-level helper-function library, GPT-4-Turbo emits Python P:S→R^k. The function returns one or more scalar subtask-progress variables plus booleans indicating whether progress means increasing or decreasing each value.

mechanisms.name: Ordered heuristic progress discretizer
mechanisms.description: The paper's D estimates a relevant range for every progress scalar, maps values to discrete features, gives later subtasks finer granularity, and adds the discrete features to form B(s)=D(P(s)). The heuristic is fixed rather than generated by the LLM.

mechanisms.name: Progress-bin count reward
mechanisms.description: Global visitation counts over B(s) define novelty proportional to inverse square-root count. The paper adds the weighted next-state novelty to a sparse extrinsic reward and trains PPO on the result.

mechanisms.name: Pinned BiDex effective reward shaper
mechanisms.description: The public shaper caches first-call extrema, adds integer-scaled progress terms, looks up 1/sqrt(global_count+1), normalizes the live batch bonus to mean 0.001, clips it to [0,0.1], replaces reward[:,0] with 0.05 times success plus bonus, and only then increments counts.

mechanisms.name: Stateful trainer-to-reward interface
mechanisms.description: RL-Games receives task success, a progress tuple in infos['binning'], relevant features, and done flags, then calls the reward shaper. Task modules compute and export the progress tuple. This interface and the shaper's state must remain fixed across reward candidates.

mechanisms.name: Best-of-four policy-sample selection
mechanisms.description: For each task, the LLM proposes multiple progress functions; a policy is trained for each, and the resulting policy with highest task success from a single training run is selected. The standard configuration uses four candidates.

mechanisms.name: Progress novelty inside NovelD
mechanisms.description: On MiniGrid, the progress-bin novelty replaces RND as NovelD's novelty estimator inside a positive temporal novelty-difference criterion gated by first episodic visit.

mechanisms.name: Full executable reward artifact boundary
mechanisms.description: Project implication: an exact ProgressCounts reward identity must bind generated P, helper library, D, count initialization and scope, update order, sparse-success evaluator, scaling, normalization, clipping, runtime versions, and the fixed trainer interface. P alone does not determine emitted rewards.

parameters.name: public_bidex_auxiliary_environment_capacity

parameters.name: public_bidex_integer_bin_mapping

parameters.name: public_bidex_count_novelty

parameters.name: public_bidex_intrinsic_clip

failure_modes.name: Direct-progress reward brittleness
failure_modes.description: Using the sum of the selected progress variables directly as dense reward averages 0.45 success versus 0.59 for count rewards over progress bins. This isolates the importance of the downstream reward transform, although the ablation has only one trial.

failure_modes.name: Generic observation hash underperformance
failure_modes.description: Replacing progress bins with SimHash over observations averages 0.34 success versus 0.59 and is no better on 19 of 20 tasks, with BlockStack within the ProgressCounts error margin.

failure_modes.name: Feature-library omission selects irrelevant state
failure_modes.description: Without the benchmark helper library, CatchUnderarm success falls from 0.76 to 0. The generated progress function averages object linear velocity, which the authors identify as irrelevant to task success, with more relevant variables.

failure_modes.name: LLM discretization range error
failure_modes.description: When the LLM generates the discrete bins instead of the fixed heuristic, SwingCup success falls from 0.97 to 0 because the generated code guesses ineffective ranges for multiple features.

failure_modes.name: Stateful and path-dependent reward identity
failure_modes.description: Global counts, first-call extrema, live-batch normalization, and update order make the same current transition emit different rewards under different histories or batching. Persisting only generated P cannot reproduce the task reward.

failure_modes.name: Paper/code binning mismatch
failure_modes.description: Appendix A.1 calls 1000 bins the default, Appendix A.9 says a two-stage allocation has 20 plus 1000 bins, and public code instead adds integer terms whose scale factors are 20 and 1020 for two stages. Addition creates collisions and is not a 20-by-1000 Cartesian encoding.

failure_modes.name: Paper/code reward-composition mismatch
failure_modes.description: Equation 1 describes sparse reward plus weighted novelty. Public BiDex code additionally normalizes by the live batch, clips to 0.1, and overwrites reward[:,0] with 0.05 times success plus the bonus rather than adding to the passed reward.

failure_modes.name: Reward-specific fixed-trainer coupling
failure_modes.description: The public reward path requires the environment to export progress and success through a specific infos contract and the trainer to maintain reward-shaper state. Retrofitting that interface per candidate changes the fixed trainer; it must exist and be frozen before comparison.

failure_modes.name: Unequal method-ablation replication
failure_modes.description: The 0.59 ProgressCounts column is averaged over five trials, while ProgressAsReward and SimHashCounts are single-trial numbers, so the table is not a variance-matched causal estimate.

failure_modes.name: Candidate-selection metric reused as endpoint
failure_modes.description: The best generated candidate is selected by policy success from a training run and success is also the reported benchmark endpoint. The paper does not describe an untouched selector holdout, so Sam requires fresh evaluation seeds and perturbations.

failure_modes.name: Unmatched TwoCatchUnderarm outer-loop budget
failure_modes.description: The paper trains four candidates for 2B samples each and selects the best, consuming 8B candidate samples. Each candidate alone matches the 2B aggregate attributed to Eureka, so the selected 0.55 result is not a fixed-total-budget comparison.

failure_modes.name: Residual standard-budget task failures
failure_modes.description: Appendix Table 8 reports success 0 for Switch, 0.03 for ReOrientation, 0.03 for PushBlock, 0.03 for TwoCatchUnderarm, and 0.05 for BlockStack under the main ProgressCounts evaluation.

failure_modes.name: Kettle result inconsistency
failure_modes.description: ProgressCounts Kettle success is 0.83 in main Table 1 but 0.99±0.01 in Appendix Table 8. Both tables label the value as ProgressCounts, and the paper does not reconcile them.

failure_modes.name: Privileged simulator-state dependence
failure_modes.description: The generation prompt permits any member of simulator self defined around observations plus helper transforms, and evaluated functions use exact object, goal, hand, and quaternion state. No physical sensing or real-robot evidence establishes deployability.

failure_modes.name: Mutable and partial public release
failure_modes.description: The official artifacts are untagged Drive files, the author project page says code is coming soon, BiDex instructions require editing a task, MiniGrid requires manually replacing a wrapper, and the supplied path starts from embedded progress functions rather than reproducing GPT proposal generation end to end.

failure_modes.name: Hard-coded release variants
failure_modes.description: The BiDex runner is fixed to Kettle until edited, and inspected task dispatch sites include no-feature or no-discretization ablation functions for some tasks. The archive therefore does not identify one machine-checkable main configuration for every table row.

evaluation.name: BiDex main comparison
evaluation.description: Across 20 tasks, ProgressCounts reports mean success 0.59, 13 percentage points above the human dense reward and 4 above Eureka. It matches or exceeds Eureka on 13 of 20 tasks and the human dense baseline on 17 of 20. The standard method selects from four 100M-sample policy candidates rather than Eureka's 80 candidates.

evaluation.name: BiDex per-task ProgressCounts results
evaluation.description: Appendix Table 8 reports mean±SD: Over .93±.01; DoorCloseInward 1.00±0; DoorCloseOutward .90±.13; DoorOpenInward .07±.15; DoorOpenOutward .99±.01; Scissors 1.00±0; SwingCup .97±.02; Switch 0±0; Kettle .99±.01; LiftUnderarm .22±.24; Pen .49±.06; BottleCap .94±.03; CatchAbreast .56±.04; CatchOver2Underarm .90±.03; CatchUnderarm .76±.05; ReOrientation .03±0; GraspAndPlace .99±.01; BlockStack .05±.05; PushBlock .03±.03; TwoCatchUnderarm .03±.02.

evaluation.name: Progress representation and reward-transform ablation
evaluation.description: Mean BiDex success is 0.59 for ProgressCounts, 0.45 for directly summed progress, and 0.34 for SimHash counts. ProgressCounts matches or exceeds direct progress on 15 of 20 tasks and SimHash on 19 of 20, but only the ProgressCounts column is averaged over five trials.

evaluation.name: Feature-library and heuristic-discretizer ablation
evaluation.description: Default/no-feature-library/no-heuristic success is SwingCup 0.97/0.90/0, CatchUnderarm 0.76/0/0.76, and DoorCloseOutward 0.90/0.86/0.92. Failures are task-specific: irrelevant velocity without the library and bad feature ranges without the heuristic.

evaluation.name: MiniGrid NovelD sample efficiency
evaluation.description: Samples in units of 10^7 for ProgressCounts/RND to cross the threshold are KeyCorridor S3R3 .2/.5, S4R3 .5/.9, S5R3 .9/1.3, S6R3 1.2/1.7; ObstructedMaze 2Dlhb 1.6/4.0, 1Q 1.0/2.8, 2Q 2.5/4.7, Full 2.9/7.2. Results average four trials; threshold is .75 except Full at .5.

evaluation.name: TwoCatchUnderarm long-budget stretch
evaluation.description: The best of four policies trained for 2B samples each reaches 0.55 success and continues improving; all extrinsic baselines and standard four-by-100M ProgressCounts are near zero. Selection consumes 8B aggregate candidate samples.

evaluation.name: Benchmark-level hyperparameter sensitivity
evaluation.description: Five-trial three-task sweeps find no single monotone trend across intrinsic coefficients 0.01/0.001/0.0001 or bin counts 500/1000/2000. The chosen 0.001 and 1000 are suboptimal on most displayed task rows, supporting a benchmark-level fixed setting but not universal robustness.

evaluation.name: Pinned public-artifact audit
evaluation.description: The exact Drive archives expose embedded progress functions and effective reward code, but the instructions require manual task/wrapper changes, the BiDex script runs Kettle by default, and the project page does not publish a versioned repository. These bytes support mechanism inspection, not turnkey reproduction of all reported results.

evidence.locator: v2 abstract metadata and submission history
evidence.claim: The record gives the title, six authors, 2024-10-25 v2 date, two-version history, active arXiv entry, and arXiv DOI.

evidence.locator: Section 4.1, Progress Function Definition and Generation
evidence.claim: P maps simulator state to one or more scalar subtask-progress values and direction booleans; generation receives state-feature descriptions, a short task description, and a benchmark helper library.
Count novelty is proportional to inverse square-root bin visitation and the paper writes total reward as sparse extrinsic reward plus lambda times next-state novelty.
D estimates ranges, discretizes later subtasks more finely, sums discrete features into B(s), and ProgressCounts trains PPO with count novelty over those bins.

BiDex has 20 tasks; success is averaged over five policy-training trials; all experiments use PPO; the LLM is gpt-4-turbo-2024-04-09; four policy samples per task are trained for 100M environment samples and the highest-success result is selected.

The authors report 0.59 average BiDex success, 13 percentage points above human dense rewards, 4 above Eureka, with four policy samples versus Eureka's 80; ProgressCounts matches or exceeds Eureka on 13 of 20 tasks and human rewards on 17 of 20.
Four ProgressCounts policies are each trained for 2B environment samples and the best reaches 0.55 success, while standard 4-by-100M ProgressCounts and extrinsic baselines remain near zero.

ProgressCounts, ProgressAsReward, and SimHashCounts average 0.59, 0.45, and 0.34; comparisons are 15 of 20 and 19 of 20 tasks; ProgressCounts uses five trials while ablations use one; Kettle is 0.83 in this table.
Default/no-feature-library/no-heuristic results are SwingCup .97/.90/0, CatchUnderarm .76/0/.76, and DoorCloseOutward .90/.86/.92.

evidence.locator: Section 5.3, environment feature engineering library ablation paragraph
evidence.claim: Without the feature library, the CatchUnderarm generator includes object linear velocity, judged irrelevant to task success, and the policy fails.
Without heuristic discretization, the LLM guesses ineffective feature ranges and SwingCup fails.
Five-trial sweeps give exact outcomes for lambda 0.01/0.001/0.0001 and bin counts 500/1000/2000; settings are chosen once per benchmark, and the appendix calls 0.001 and 1000 the defaults.
Progress novelty is inserted into NovelD and evaluated for four trials on eight MiniGrid tasks; the table gives exact threshold sample counts and reports up to 64% improvement over RND.

The prompt allows one or two task stages, averaging multiple variables per stage, and access to members of simulator self; the BiDex and MiniGrid helper libraries each contain three specified functions.
The paper supplies example heuristic discretization code used to map continuous progress variables to bins.
The table reports exact mean and standard deviation for ProgressCounts across all 20 BiDex tasks and lists Kettle as 0.99±0.01.

evidence.locator: Appendix A.9, Code, Hyperparameters, and Compute
evidence.claim: The paper links the anonymous Drive artifacts, names the Eureka and NovelD bases, gives BiDex scale .05 and intrinsic mean .001, 20/1000 two-stage bin allocation and 1020 total, MiniGrid coefficient .5 and 50 bins, and reports eight V100 GPUs over three weeks.

evidence.locator: official author project page, Code section
evidence.claim: The project page summarizes the paper but displays Code (coming soon), so it does not identify a versioned public repository.

DefaultRewardsShaper allocates 100000 CUDA count slots and 2048-row auxiliary state, caches first-call extrema, uses additive 20/1020 progress scaling, computes 1/sqrt(count+1), normalizes to mean .001, clips to .1, writes .05*success plus bonus, then increments global counts; its dormant NovelD branch initializes alpha .5.
